title: Auditory ossicles
source: OpenStax A&P 2e: 14.1 Sensory Perception; 7.2 The Skull

main.t: The three tiny bones of the middle ear: the malleus, incus and stapes (auditory ossicles).

simpler.t: The ossicles are three tiny bones in your ear that pass sound inwards.

deeper.t: Their Latin names roughly mean hammer, anvil and stirrup.

facts.t: They span the space of the middle ear, inside the petrous part of the temporal bone.
The malleus is attached to the eardrum (tympanic membrane).
The stapes is attached to the inner ear, at the oval window of the cochlea.

simpler.t: They sit deep in your ear, between the eardrum and the inner ear.

deeper.t: The ear canal leading to the eardrum enters the skull through the external acoustic meatus.

items.name: Malleus
items.t: “Hammer”: attached to the eardrum, and joined to the incus.

items.name: Incus
items.t: “Anvil”: between the other two, joined to both.

items.name: Stapes
items.t: “Stirrup”: joined to the incus, and attached to the inner ear at the oval window.

items.name: A chain of joints
items.t: The three are joined end to end, from the eardrum to the inner ear.

items.name: Footplate of the stapes
items.t: Its flat base fills the oval window.

simpler.t: They are a chain of three tiny bones: hammer, anvil and stirrup.

deeper.t: The stapes is the smallest bone in the body.

facts.t: Sound makes the eardrum vibrate; the ossicles pass the vibrations along to the inner ear.
Vibrations passing through the oval window set the fluid of the cochlea moving in waves.
The fluid waves match the frequencies of the sound.

simpler.t: They pass the eardrum’s vibrations along to the fluid of the inner ear.

items.name: Tympanic membrane (eardrum)
items.t: Vibrates when sound strikes it; the malleus is attached to it.

items.name: Cochlea
items.t: The inner ear organ of hearing, attached to the stapes through the oval window.

items.name: Round window
items.t: A membrane-covered opening that bulges as the fluid in the cochlea moves.

items.name: Temporal bone
items.t: Its petrous part contains the middle and inner ear.

items.name: Vestibulocochlear nerve
items.t: Carries the signals of hearing from the cochlea to the brainstem.

simpler.t: They link the eardrum to the cochlea, deep in the temporal bone.

facts.t: They form from cartilage of the embryonic pharyngeal arches.

items.injury: Abnormal bone growth fixes the stapes in the oval window (otosclerosis).
items.cannotDo: Hear well: sound is no longer passed into the inner ear.
items.why: The stapes must move to send vibrations through the oval window.
items.check: Otosclerosis is not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–9, 12–16, 20); the role of the oval window is.

items.injury: A blast, or something pushed into the ear canal.
items.why: The malleus is attached to the eardrum, which must vibrate to move the ossicles.
items.check: A torn eardrum is not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–9, 12–16, 20); the eardrum’s role is.

items.q: Explain how sound reaches the inner ear.
model: Sound waves travel down the ear canal and strike the eardrum, which vibrates.
The malleus, attached to the eardrum, passes the vibration to the incus.
The incus passes it to the stapes.
The stapes moves the oval window, sending waves through the fluid of the cochlea.

items.q: Compare the attachments of the malleus and the stapes.
model: The malleus is attached to the eardrum, at the outer end of the chain.
The stapes is attached to the inner ear, at the oval window.
So vibration passes from the outer to the inner ear.

items.q: Predict the effect on hearing if the stapes cannot move, and explain it.
model: The stapes cannot move the oval window.
So little vibration reaches the fluid of the cochlea.
The sound-sensing cells are hardly stimulated.
items.check: Hearing loss from a fixed stapes is not in OpenStax A&P 2e (chapters 6–9, 12–16, 20); the role of the oval window is.

check.stem: Which ossicle is attached to the eardrum?
check.why: The malleus is attached to the tympanic membrane.

check.stem: Which ossicle is attached to the oval window?
check.why: The cochlea is attached to the stapes through the oval window.

check.stem: Which bone houses the middle ear?
check.why: Cavities inside the petrous part of the temporal bone house the middle and inner ears.
